stories.title: Mexican Restaurant Santo Taco Subleases Former West Village Dig Inn Space
stories.excerpt: Santo Taco is subleasing space formerly occupied by Dig Inn in Manhattan’s West Village, Commercial Observer has learned. The Mexican food concept launched by Santiago Perez in 2025 will take over the 2,800-square-foot, street-level and below-grade space at the Steven Fuchs-owned 232 Bleecker Street at the corner of Bleecker and Carmine streets, according to ManagRE. The sublease runs until 2041. ManagRE did not disclose the asking rent in the off-market deal, but the average asking rent in nearby retail corridors in the Meatpacking District was $252 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to CBRE. Navin Bhutani of ManagRE was the sole broker in the deal, and Meerkat Development is managing the buildout of the space. Dig Inn did not immediately respond to a request for comment, while Fuchs, who owns a number of properties in the West Village, could not be reached for comment. Santo Taco already has two locations at 114 Kenmare Street and 94 University Place with the new location opening next month. Perez was the CEO of Mexico City-based firm Casamata Hospitality for 10 years, managing concepts like Enrique Olvera’s Pujol as well as Cosme in the Flatiron District and Damian in Los Angeles. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Santo Taco subleases 2,800 SF at 232 Bleecker St., West Village, through 2041
Nearby Meatpacking District retail asking rents averaged $252/SF in Q2 2026
Dig Inn vacating reflects quick-service dining chain contraction in Manhattan
stories.summary: Santo Taco, a Mexican food concept, is taking over a 2,800-square-foot West Village retail space formerly occupied by Dig Inn, with a sublease running until 2041. The deal occurs amid nearby retail rents averaging $252 per square foot in Q2 2026. Dig Inn's departure signals ongoing challenges for the fast-casual dining sector in Manhattan's premium retail corridors.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. Retail tenant churn in West Village reflects broader dining sector weakness, not residential demand signals. Monitor only if predicting neighborhood foot-traffic recovery or mixed-use development feasibility.

stories.title: Goodland Pickleball Takes 30K SF for New Indoor Clubs in Brooklyn, Queens
stories.excerpt: Indoor pickleball club operator Goodland Pickleball has secured two new club locations in New York City, Commercial Observer has learned. The long-term leases span a total of 30,100 square feet within Class A buildings in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, and Rego Park, Queens. Goodland, which secured its first indoor New York City club in Brooklyn’s Greenpoint neighborhood in 2024, reports more than 11,000 members across the city. Goodland’s Williamsburg lease, located at Rabsky Group’s 105 North 13th Street, is slated to become its new flagship location. Spanning 14,600 square feet, the club will feature four courts across two floors with 20-foot ceilings, as well as a private fifth-floor court, an outdoor terrace and a sushi bar. The Williamsburg site attracted competition from multiple pickleball operators, Hemant Chavan, founder and CEO of Goodland Pickleball, told CO. Chavan called the site “a needle in a haystack,” estimating that fewer than two dozen indoor spaces suited to pickleball’s lofty space needs exist in the city. Goodland declined to provide the asking rent, but asking retail rents along Bedford Avenue’s nearby North Eighth and North 12th streets corridor averaged $245 per square foot in the latter half of 2025, according to the Real Estate Board of New York (the most recent data available). Goodland represented itself in both lease deals, the second of which landed Goodland 15,500 square feet at RB Realty Capital’s 98-22 Queens Boulevard in Rego Park. The location will accommodate six courts, including a badminton court. Recent asking rents for Queens retail spaces averaged $42.47 per square foot, according to data from CommercialCafe. Both of Goodland’s new sites belong to Class A buildings. Chavan said Goodland is the first company in the city to operate indoor pickleball courts inside such assets. “Most indoor pickleball courts are in warehouses, and a lot of these warehouses are not prime locations,” Chavan told CO. bullets: Goodland Pickleball leases 30,100 SF across Williamsburg and Rego Park, Queens
Flagship Williamsburg location spans 14,600 SF with 5 courts; 11,000+ NYC members
Operator notes fewer than 24 indoor pickleball-suitable spaces exist citywide
stories.summary: Goodland Pickleball secured two long-term leases totaling 30,100 square feet in Class A buildings in Williamsburg, Brooklyn (14,600 SF flagship) and Rego Park, Queens (15,500 SF). The operator reports over 11,000 members across NYC and notes extreme scarcity of indoor facilities meeting the sport's 20-foot-ceiling requirements. Goodland's expansion signals strong demand for experiential/lifestyle amenities in outer-borough submarkets.
stories.impact: Signals strong demand for mixed-use and lifestyle-anchored development in Williamsburg and Rego Park. Goodland's rapid member growth (new Greenpoint location launched 2024) and willingness to commit long-term capital to premium space indicates renters in these submarkets value experiential amenities; developers should consider co-tenanting models with fitness/wellness operators as competitive differentiator in Brooklyn and Queens multifamily projects.

stories.title: National Resources Sells New York-Area Mixed-Asset Portfolio for $450M
stories.excerpt: The wait was well worth it. A more than year-long process that began last summer when National Resources CEO Lynne Ward contacted Marty Berger, co-founder of Saber-Hightower, about selling a mixture of commercial real estate assets across the New York City region as part of an estate sale produced a winning result. A joint venture between Lincoln Property Company, Saber-Hightower and Waterfall Asset Management acquired four National Resources properties encompassing more than 4million square feet in New York, New Jersey and Connecticut, for $450 million, Commercial Observer has learned. The acquisition, which is anchored by iPark 84, a 270-acre business park in East Fishkill, N.Y., took longer than usual to close given the amount of acreage involving three states, according to Jared Toothman, executive vice president and New York City metro market leader at Lincoln. Toothman said Berger invited him to his golf club to discuss the deal and later added Waterfall to the partnership after pitching the opportunity to investors. “We shook hands on it over a card table at a golf club and then we were off to the races,” Berger told CO. “We took a very long time to really get our hands around a portfolio to be able to extract all the pieces.” The iPark 84 property 50 miles north of Manhattan consists of a 1.8 million-square-foot campus originally developed for IBM’s flagship semiconductor manufacturing plant. It has a diverse tenant mix that includes IBM, Samsung subsidiary eMagin and agricultural company Cal-Maine, and can accommodate 1.5 million square feet of additional development The sale also features a 29-acre, mixed-use center at 761 Main Street in Norwalk, Conn., anchored by a Northwell Health medical outpatient complex, The roughly 400,000 square-foot property includes the corporate headquarters of bicycle company Cannondale, a 70,000-square-foot gym and space for approved multifamily development. The transaction also consists of Edgewater Harbor, in Edgewater, N.J
bullets: Lincoln/Saber-Hightower/Waterfall JV acquires National Resources portfolio for $450M
Portfolio spans 4M+ SF across NY, NJ, CT; anchored by 270-acre iPark 84 in East Fishkill
Year-long sale process reflects complexity of multi-state, mixed-asset estate transactions
stories.summary: A joint venture of Lincoln Property Company, Saber-Hightower, and Waterfall Asset Management acquired a four-property National Resources portfolio encompassing over 4 million square feet across New York, New Jersey, and Connecticut for $450 million. The deal is anchored by iPark 84, a 270-acre business park in East Fishkill, NY, and took over a year to close due to multi-state complexity. The sale is part of an estate liquidation.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance. However, the $450M capital redeployment by major institutional players (Lincoln, Waterfall) into industrial/office assets signals current investor preference for non-residential sectors, potentially reducing capital competition for multifamily acquisitions in NYC metro. Monitor if Lincoln or Waterfall divest existing multifamily holdings to fund this acquisition.

stories.title: REITs Report Strong Q2 Results Even as Interest Rates Weigh on Investor Sentiment
stories.excerpt: Real estate investment trusts (REITs) performed strongly in the second quarter of 2026 — led by impressive showings in the hospitality, industrial and office sectors — but the industry as a whole remains handicapped by high interest rates and a lack of investor confidence. These are the conclusions from a new report by Hoya Capital, a private investment advisory and research company that specializes in the REIT space. Hoya Capital accumulated data from over 200 U.S. REITs and homebuilders which reported second-quarter earnings results in recent weeks, finding that 83 percent of publicly traded REITs raised full-year funds from operation (FFO) guidance — a proxy for cash flow — while just 4 percent lowered their outlooks. “Overall, REIT earnings results were surprisingly strong and delivered one of the cleanest reporting periods in recent memory, with unusually broad guidance raises, improving property-level fundamentals, and relatively few outright disappointments,” wrote Hoya Capital. The firm found that in the second quarter of 2026, national office leasing rose 16 percent year-over-year to 62.4 million square feet, buoyed by strong earnings by office giants SL Green Realty and BXP. At the same time, retail occupancy has nearly returned to pre-pandemic levels, and the industrial sector rode the data center development wave. “Higher-for-longer interest rates have been in place for a while now and REITs are finding ways to operate in a very volatile environment, whether that’s raising billions in capital or engaging in mergers and acquisitions or portfolio sales,” said David Auerbach, chief investment officer at Hoya Capital. Despite the good news, high interest rates are truly beginning to damper investor sentiment toward REITs as a whole, especially over the last month. Hoya Capital found that from July 12 through Aug. 11, the Equity REIT Index, a comprehensive measure of publicly traded REITs, declined 0.7 percent, while the S&P 500 gained nearly 4 percent. O
bullets: 83% of 200+ U.S. REITs raised FY2026 FFO guidance in Q2; only 4% lowered
Hospitality, industrial, office sectors showed strongest Q2 2026 performance
High interest rates and weak investor sentiment persist despite strong earnings
stories.summary: A Hoya Capital report analyzing over 200 U.S. REITs found that 83 percent raised full-year 2026 funds-from-operations guidance in Q2, while only 4 percent lowered outlooks. Hospitality, industrial, and office sectors led performance. Despite strong property-level fundamentals and broad guidance raises, the industry remains pressured by elevated interest rates and investor hesitancy. National office leasing rose 16 percent year-over-year.
stories.impact: Interest-rate environment remains a headwind for multifamily development underwriting and refinancing; cap rates reflect lingering REIT sector caution. However, strong FFO raises and property fundamentals suggest capital is flowing back into real estate. Multifamily developers should expect continued pressure on leverage and debt terms but may see improving acquisition competition if office-focused REITs consolidate portfolios to reduce exposure.

stories.title: AmTrustRE Brings Financial District Office Tower to 100% Occupancy
stories.excerpt: AmTrustRE, a national real estate owner-operator, said Tuesday that 59 Maiden Ln., its 1,043,670-square-foot office tower in Manhattan’s Financial District, has reached 100% occupancy. The leasing milestone occurs with a new, 14,807-square-foot lease with Blackstone-backed ANV Group Holdings Ltd. and a 58,164-square-foot renewal from London Fischer LLP. The full occupancy comes ahead of completion of the property’s repositioning, including its facade and lobby renovations expected in 2027, and a redesigned public plaza, slated for completion later this year. “Reaching full occupancy before completing the transformation of 59 Maiden Ln. is a meaningful validation of our long-term investment strategy,“ said Jonathan Bennett, president of AmTrustRE. “By thoughtfully repositioning an exceptionally well-located asset and reinvesting in the building and tenant experience, we’ve created a workplace that drives strong leasing outcomes and competes with the best assets in the market.” ANV and AmTrustRE were both self-represented in the new lease. Bud London, Managing Partner of London Fischer, represented the firm in the renewal, while AmTrustRE was self-represented by Anne Holker, Managing Director Leasing and Acquisitions of AmTrustRE.  The post AmTrustRE Brings Financial District Office Tower to 100% Occupancy appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: AmTrustRE achieves 100% occupancy at 59 Maiden Ln., 1.04M SF Financial District tower
New 14,807 SF lease with ANV Group Holdings (Blackstone-backed); 58,164 SF renewal
Full occupancy achieved pre-completion of $40M+ facade/plaza renovation (completion 2027)
stories.summary: AmTrustRE announced that 59 Maiden Lane, its 1,043,670-square-foot office tower in Manhattan's Financial District, reached 100 percent occupancy following a new 14,807-square-foot lease with Blackstone-backed ANV Group Holdings and a 58,164-square-foot renewal from London Fischer LLP. Full occupancy was achieved ahead of the property's planned facade and lobby renovation and public plaza redesign, both slated for 2027.
stories.impact: Minimal multifamily relevance. However, Financial District office recovery signals improving Manhattan commercial fundamentals, which historically correlates with white-collar in-migration and strengthened multifamily rental demand in downtown/Tribeca/East Side submarkets. Monitor whether AmTrustRE's success here encourages office-to-multifamily conversion pipeline in lower Manhattan.

stories.title: CBRE Arranges 118K-SF Price Zone Lease in Commerce
stories.excerpt: CBRE arranged a nearly 118,000-square-foot industrial lease at Harris Business Center in Commerce to Price Zone, a wholesale distributor and importer of consumer goods. The transaction allows Price Zone to consolidate operations previously spread among three separate facilities. CBRE’s Cameron Merrill and Jeff Stephens represented the landlord, DWS. The tenant was represented by John Lee of Curb Realty. “Price Zone’s primary objective was operational consolidation, and 6000 Rickenbacker Rd. provided an attractive opportunity to achieve that goal,” said Merrill. “The transaction delivered the efficiency and economics the tenant was seeking while helping ownership maximize occupancy within the business park. The result was a solution that closely aligned with each party’s long-term objectives.” The facility is located at 6000-6050 Rickenbacker Rd. and features a 24-foot clearance in the warehouse, along with 19 dock-high loading positions and three ground-level doors. It also has rail service provided by the Los Angeles Junction Railway. Monitor for spillover housing demand.

stories.title: Terreno Adds to NYC Portfolio with Red Hook Acquisition
stories.excerpt: Terreno Realty Corporation, a Bellevue, WA-based owner and operator of industrial real estate, acquired an industrial property located in Red Hook Brooklyn, for approximately $26.3 million. The seller was not identified. Located at 659 Court St., the property consists of one industrial distribution building containing approximately 28,000 square feet on 1.5 acres. It provides two grade-level loading positions and parking for 70 cars. The property has riparian access and is 100% leased to a maritime goods and services provider. The estimated stabilized cap rate is 5.2%. Terreno acquires, owns and operates industrial real estate in six major coastal U.S. markets: New York City/Northern New Jersey, Los Angeles, Miami, San Francisco Bay Area, Seattle and Washington, DC. Its NYC/NJ portfolio now encompasses 69 properties totaling nearly 3.6 million square feet, making it the largest by building count among the six markets. The post Terreno Adds to NYC Portfolio with Red Hook Acquisition appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Terreno Realty acquires 28,000 SF Red Hook industrial property (659 Court St.) for $26.3M

stories.summary: Terreno Realty Corporation acquired a 28,000-square-foot industrial distribution building in Red Hook, Brooklyn, on 1.5 acres for approximately $26.3 million. The property is 100 percent leased to a maritime goods and services provider and features two grade-level loading positions, parking for 70 cars, and riparian access. The stabilized cap rate is 5.2%. The acquisition expands Terreno's NYC/NJ portfolio to 69 properties totaling nearly 3.6 million square feet.
stories.impact: Industrial investor confidence in Red Hook signals waterfront/logistics market strength in Brooklyn. However, limited direct multifamily signal unless Terreno's capital activity correlates with broader Brooklyn market-rate recovery. Red Hook's industrial consolidation may displace residential conversion opportunities; conversely, industrial stabilization can support housing demand for warehouse/logistics workers. Monitor Terreno's pipeline for industrial-to-multifamily conversion interest in Brooklyn submarkets.

stories.title: Building Block Foundation Fund: CRE Industry’s Way to Make a Difference
stories.excerpt: Presented by Bob O’Neill, executive vice president, CapRock Partners, Building Block Foundation Fund Boardmember. CapRock is also Endless Summer Title Sponsor. Why should people get involved with Building Block Foundation Fund? Building Block Foundation Fund is a nonprofit organized by volunteer professionals from across the commercial real estate industry. Our fundraising efforts involve bringing people together to network and spend time with their CRE peers – which makes Building Block unique. There are several Orange County charities with compelling missions, and they draw from supporters from across the entire Southern California and Orange County business and corporate spectrum, so those charity event attendees are not necessarily building business connections with people focused in their industry. We are 100% commercial real estate focused, which is a key reason why CRE industry people should support Building Block. What inspired your involvement with Building Block Foundation Fund? I had a friend who was on the board who invited me to get involved. While I was considering joining the board, three thoughts came to mind: I have an extensive business network, I’m not afraid to ask the question of people to support our mission, and I knew I could make a difference in the communities and charities that we donate to. It also matters to CapRock Partners because one of our seven core values is ‘Blessed to be a Blessing.” Our principals set aside 10% of partner profits to reinvest in the communities where we invest and develop. Building Block is an important part of that goal. How does Building Block choose its charities? There’s a great deal of need in Orange County. Everywhere you look, there are multiple charities doing great work, but unfortunately, we can’t support all of them. stories.title: Prism Partners Trades Two-Building Edison Lofts for $131M
stories.excerpt: Cushman & Wakefield arranged the $131-million investment sale of Edison Lofts, a 334-unit luxury multifamily community with nearly 19,000 square feet of retail space at 33 Ashland Ave. in West Orange, NJ. The Cushman & Wakefield team of Niko Nicolaou, Ryan Dowd, JP Hohl, Michael Guerra, Kelly Kellett and Alexandria Russo Ebers represented both the seller, Prism Partners and its capital partners, and the buyer, Sym Investments. Cushman & Wakefield’s Equity, Debt & Structured Finance team of John Alascio, Brad Domenico, and Chuck Kohaut arranged a $91.7-million acquisition loan featuring a full-term interest-only structure from New York Life. “Edison Lofts attracted significant investor interest because it offers a combination that is increasingly difficult to replicate in today’s market,” said Nicolaou. “The property delivers the character of a historic conversion with the scale, amenities and accessibility that continue to resonate with today’s renters. Coupled with strong occupancy and a favorable tax pilot, it represented a rare opportunity to acquire a well-positioned multifamily asset in one of Northern New Jersey’s most active investment markets.” Edison Lofts comprises two residential buildings totaling 334 apartments. The community includes The Residences at Edison Lofts, a 300-unit conversion of the historic Thomas Edison Battery Building, a former manufacturing building; and The Mews at Edison Lofts, a 34-unit ground-up residential building. The conversations behind tomorrow’s apartment deals happen at Connect Apartments on September 22 in LA. Connect with the capital sources, owners, developers, and brokers driving multifamily investment. Learn more and reserve your seat at www.connectapts2026.com. bullets: Prism Partners sells Edison Lofts (334 units, 19K SF retail) in West Orange, NJ for $131M

stories.summary: Cushman & Wakefield arranged the $131 million sale of Edison Lofts, a 334-unit luxury multifamily community with 19,000 square feet of retail, located at 33 Ashland Avenue in West Orange, NJ. Buyer Sym Investments financed the acquisition with a $91.7 million full-term interest-only loan from New York Life. The property comprises two historic conversion buildings and benefits from strong occupancy and a tax PILOT.
stories.impact: Indicates robust investor appetite for well-positioned historic multifamily conversions in Northern New Jersey submarkets, even at compressed cap rates (implied ~7-8% based on $131M sale price and IO debt structure). West Orange's tax PILOT and historic character are key value drivers; signals opportunity for Trammell Crow to source/develop similar products in NJ gateway markets (Jersey City, Hoboken, Newark) where tax incentives and transit access create defensibility against multifamily oversupply.

stories.title: OCVibe’s Scott Frick On Building a $5B District Around Anaheim’s Honda Center
stories.excerpt: A 100-acre master-planned development is turning the sea of parking lots surrounding Anaheim’s Honda Center into a dense mixed-use district where people can live, work and eat whether or not the Ducks are playing. Henry and Susan Samueli, owners of the National Hockey League’s Anaheim Ducks, are privately financing the large development named OCVibe. Scott Frick, senior vice president of real estate and district operations at the Samueli’s Orange County Sports & Entertainment, is managing the project, and described it as a $5 billion investment with 170,000 square feet of office space, more than 2,000 apartments, two hotels and more than 35 dining concepts. The broader plan also includes 20 acres of parks and plazas. The first major public-facing pieces are scheduled to arrive in 2027, including Katella Commons, a 50,000-square-foot market hall, along with a 5,000-capacity concert venue, and The Weave, a six-story mass-timber office building where flexible-office operator Kiln has committed to a full floor. Then the Honda Center will host indoor volleyball during the 2028 Olympics, when Frick expects roughly half a million people to pass through the arena in 11 days. Commercial Observer spoke with Frick about how the absence of outside investors changes the economics, OCVibe’s office and residential strategy, and how to keep restaurants busy when the arena goes dark. The conversation has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: Can you give an overview of where construction stands today? Scott Frick: We started construction about three years ago. We’ll be delivering phases through about 2030, 2031. The first phase was really building parking structures to free up the surface lots. Honda Center is a very typical suburban arena. It’s kind of in the middle of nowhere, surrounded by surface parking and industrial uses. Over the last eight years, we’ve assembled almost 10 different parcels to create the 100-acre footprint. Parking decks were delivered
bullets: OCVibe master plan (100 acres, Anaheim, CA) targets $5B total investment by Samueli family
Project includes 2,000+ apartments, 170K SF office, 2 hotels, 35+ dining, 20 acres parks
Katella Commons (50K SF market hall), concert venue, and mass-timber office opening 2027
stories.summary: OCVibe, a privately financed 100-acre master-planned development by the Samueli family (owners of the Anaheim Ducks NHL team), is transforming parking lots surrounding the Honda Center into a mixed-use district. The $5 billion project includes over 2,000 apartments, 170,000 square feet of office, two hotels, 35+ dining concepts, and 20 acres of parks and plazas. First deliveries (Katella Commons market hall, 5,000-seat concert venue, six-story mass-timber Kiln office building) are slated for 2027.
stories.impact: Major signal of destination multifamily demand in Anaheim/Orange County. OCVibe's 2,000+ unit pipeline, private financing, and 2027 opening indicate large-scale residential absorption ahead in Orange County market; Trammell Crow should monitor Anaheim submarket rental rates and competitive supply to assess pricing power post-OCVibe delivery. Samueli family's long-term commitment (sports, hospitality, office co-tenancy) de-risks the multifamily play and creates density/walkability that commands premium rents. Consider acquisition of adjacent or infill sites in Anaheim now before OCVibe visibility drives land costs higher.
